turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Observations and this morning's bloods are here if you want them straight off.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Go on.

[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure's one forty eight over eighty six, pulse seventy two. Creatinine one hundred and forty eight, eGFR forty two. It was fifty two last time. My dad's diabetic too, he has a proper strop at every blood test, so I do feel for him.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sit. What's the problem.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): There isn't a problem. Umm, just the kidney check. I'm alright.
[SEG0006] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He's not, umm, he's not alright. The knees have been agony, he can hardly get to the corner shop.
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Oh give over. Bit of an ache if I walk to the shops. Nothing.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Painkillers.
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Err, ibuprofen from the shop. Four hundred milligrams when it niggles. Not often.
[SEG0010] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Most days, if I'm honest.
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): It is not most days. Couple of times a week. Hardly counts.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Regular tablets.

[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Amlodipine five milligrams in the morning for the pressure. Atorvastin for the cholesterol, twenty milligrams at night. Metformin for the sugar, five hundred milligrams twice a day. Only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning as well, a teaspoon for the joints, and I stopped the bendroflumethiazide in March, didn't suit me.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ramipril.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Still on it. Two and a half. Morning.
[SEG0016] person_4 (CAREGIVER): They offered him alendronic acid for the bones once. He never took a single one.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then it doesn't go on the list. Chest pain? Breathlessness?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Waterworks? Bowels?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Fine. All of it.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ankles.
[SEG0022] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Swollen a fortnight. I've been on at him.
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): They're not swollen. Little bit puffy last night. That's it.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): So somewhere between last night and a fortnight. Let me look. Mild puffiness, no pitting.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): The ibuprofen clamps down the blood flow in the kidneys, that's why the creatinine's up. Diabetes dulls the warning signs on top, but the numbers don't lie.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stop the ibuprofen. Paracetamol, one gram, up to four times a day, for the knee. Keep the ramipril.
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Paracetamol's useless. But yeah, whatever you say.
[SEG0028] person_4 (CAREGIVER): My sister's been on dialysis three years. I can't help thinking of her when they read those numbers.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Different thing entirely. Repeat kidney bloods in one week. Back here in four weeks. If the creatinine hasn't come down we'll refer to renal then, not today.
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): We done?
[SEG0031] person_1 (NURSE): I'll book the blood test at the desk.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. And bin that ibuprofen when you get home.
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm. Fine.
[SEG0034] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll see it goes. He tucks things at the back of the cupboard.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good.

spec.situation: Older diabetic with kidney disease on review; creatinine and eGFR read aloud; takes ibuprofen from a shop against advice; ramipril continued, painkiller advice changed.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Puffiness present, but duration is disputed; certainty 'certain' overstates transcript disagreement.
bad.text: ankle puffiness (category=cardiovascular, status=present, duration=approximately 1 day to 2 weeks, temporality=current, body_site=ankles, reported_by=caregiver, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Dose and frequency supported, but indication 'knee pain' not explicitly stated by patient.
bad.text: ibuprofen (dose=400 mg, frequency=a couple of times a week, indication=knee pain, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

eGFR result completed and presented by nurse, but not 'requested_by nurse'.

Caregiver reported ibuprofen use as 'most days', conflicting with the patient's report of a couple of times a week.
Doctor documented/said not to list alendronic acid because although it had once been offered for the bones, the patient 'never took a single one'.
